mcat_description.short: MS Bunkhouse is a prefabricated mild steel portable cabin structure used as temporary accommodation for workers and staff at construction sites, industrial projects, and remote worksites. Sold as complete modular units, customisable in dimensions, with insulation, doors, windows, and basic electrical fittings included.
mcat_description.long: An MS (Mild Steel) Bunkhouse is a factory-fabricated, relocatable accommodation unit constructed from a mild steel structural frame with steel sheet cladding, insulated wall and roof panels (glass wool or PUF), and fitted with aluminium sliding windows, steel or aluminium doors, false flooring, and concealed electrical wiring. Units are manufactured using MIG (CO2 argon shield gas) welding and finished with epoxy zinc phosphate primer and synthetic epoxy topcoats for corrosion and weather resistance. They are designed as lift-and-shift structures transportable by trailer, enabling rapid deployment and relocation across project sites without permanent foundation work. Buyers typically configure units as sleeping dormitories, site offices, mess units, toilet blocks, security cabins, or combined accommodation complexes for labour camps at construction, infrastructure, and industrial projects.

market_context: In the Indian B2B market, 'MS Bunkhouse' is a well-established trade term for a mild steel prefabricated portable cabin used primarily as temporary worker accommodation at construction, infrastructure, and industrial project sites. The 'MS' prefix (Mild Steel) is a distinctly Indian trade qualifier distinguishing these units from GI (galvanised iron), FRP, ACP, or PUF-panel variants. Manufacturers are concentrated in Maharashtra (Thane, Mumbai, Raigad, Badlapur), Karnataka (Bengaluru), Gujarat (Vadodara), Uttar Pradesh (Greater Noida, Delhi NCR), Telangana (Hyderabad), and Odisha (Bhubaneswar), reflecting demand from construction activity across India. Units are fabricated using MIG (CO2 argon shield gas) welding, finished with epoxy zinc phosphate primer and synthetic epoxy topcoats, and insulated with glass wool (25 mm walls, 50 mm roof) or PUF panels. The product is designed as a lift-and-shift structure transportable by trailer, with size constrained by trailer dimensions. Buyers include construction contractors, infrastructure developers, industrial plant operators, and government/defence procurement agencies. The MCAT sits within the broader 'Prefabricated Structures' taxonomy alongside portable toilets, site offices, and greenhouses — all distinct product types sharing the same prefab construction method. No BIS/IS standard specific to MS bunkhouses was identified; quality is governed by material grades (IS 2062 mild steel) and paint/insulation specifications set by manufacturers and buyers contractually.
